**Ruling text of record · 2026-11-26T20:02Z** (adds to 7200732942 and 7201405662; closes review N13 of PR #37606, record 7201298747)

The maintainer's answer recorded in 7200732942 was, in its original language, 「全部按推荐」 ("all as recommended", 2026-11-26 18:39Z). The recommendations it adopted, as put to the maintainer:
- **▲1** The system identity is not bound by the closed-state lock; users and admins are. The author docs must state that an action body runs as system, so any action that edits the record still takes effect on a closed one unless its own body checks the state.
- **▲2** A closed record cannot be deleted by any user, whatever their delete permission; a pending (not closed) record deletes as today.
- **▲3** Item ③ of the 11-22 ruling applies to `readonlyWhen` field locks only; the record lock judges the stored state at write time.
- **▲4** A new data-layer "is it locked" read; the approvals lock read stays as published. A card to retire or redirect the approvals read is filed with the build cards.
- **5** Every caller who can read the record is told `locked` and the reason; the ADR states the one bit of the state field this discloses and why.
- **10** A cascade delete is judged as a whole before its first write; its refusal names only the record the user asked to delete (by the title served to that user) and the blocking object's type label, stated as an explicit exception.
- **7** A new approval round stays a way out of a closed state, with the submitter's own recall spelled out. Refined at 19:16Z by 7201405662: 「平台堵住：撤回不恢复关闭值」 — the option read 「ADR 加一条：撤回永远不把状态写回关闭值」 ("the ADR adds a rule: a recall never writes the state back to a closed value").
- **6, 8, 9, 11** and the consequences listed (no grace period on publish; mirror write-back failure gets its own child card; overlay add/shorten of closed states verified by the spec card; change of owner refused on a closed record) take effect as the ADR writes them.
